title: For centuries the chess queen was the weakest piece on the board
cover:
The weakest piece
on the board.

scenes.text: The queen is the most powerful piece in chess. But for centuries it was the weakest on the board.
In medieval chess it could move just one square diagonally. It was a counsellor, not a queen.
In the late fifteenth century everything changes: the queen and the bishop gain the long moves they have today.
The first printed book on that new game is written by Lucena, a student at Salamanca, in 1497 at the latest. He calls it the queen's chess.
In Italy it got another name: alla rabiosa. The furious way.
Did Spain invent it? Nobody knows who first moved the queen that way. What we do know is where it was first printed.
Share it with the person who always beats you at chess.
